audit_question.question: When handleAcceptReply consumes an equal-ballot AcceptReply, what establishes that the counted response represents acceptance of this instance's candidate commands by a distinct participant in the current attempt, rather than only a report of the recipient's current ballot?
audit_question.importance: Repeated replies from one participant could reach the local commitment threshold without the intended number of supporting participants. A ballot report retaining different commands could also be interpreted too strongly. Either would undermine the acceptance support used to authorize commitment; divergent decisions, durability failures, and client-visible consequences remain unestablished.
participants: Shared peer transport and RPC dispatcher
objects: Per-instance commands, bal, vbal, and status
Leader bookkeeping prepareOKs, acceptOKs, and lastTriedBallot
contexts: One instance and its current acceptance attempt
Additional equal-ballot PrepareReply deliveries after the prepare threshold
Multiple Accept broadcasts for the same instance and ballot
Accept handling with existing accepted or committed state
Transport delivery and actual quorum configuration remain unresolved
event_paths: Prepare threshold reached -> Accept broadcast -> another equal-ballot PrepareReply -> another Accept broadcast -> one recipient handles both requests -> equal-ballot replies increment the same acceptOKs counter
Candidate command installation -> recipient guards and retained state -> AcceptReply construction -> ballot comparison -> local commitment threshold
Execution recovery request -> recover reuses existing bookkeeping -> makeBallot and Prepare broadcast -> reply processing
counterevidence: The run loop serially dispatches protocol handlers, so repeated broadcasts can be investigated without assuming concurrent execution of those handlers.
Each bcastAccept invocation visits at most N-1 peer-order entries and skips peers marked not alive. Distinct entries and transport behavior still require source inspection.
handleAccept installs incoming commands for missing or eligible noncommitted records; those replies follow actual command installation.
handleAccept rejects lower ballots and preserves committed records. An equal-ballot report with different retained commands still requires a justified reachable history.

handleAcceptReply ignores lower-ballot replies, treats higher ballots as nacks, and returns for committed instances. These checks restrict counting but do not visibly distinguish contributors before commitment.
handlePropose initializes fresh counters, and recover initializes counters when bookkeeping is absent. Existing bookkeeping is reused by recover.

A repeated response is consequential to distinct-participant support only when the applicable write threshold requires more distinct remote participants than have actually accepted. The deployed threshold remains to be verified.
Shared transport or dispatch filtering could constrain the suspected sequence and remains unread.
unknowns: Whether a legally reachable committed recipient can report the attempted ballot while retaining commands different from the current candidate.
Whether one instance and ballot always identifies one command batch across prepare completion, retry, recovery, and intervening handlers.
Whether the shared transport and RPC dispatcher deliver separately generated replies from repeated Accept broadcasts without contributor filtering.
Whether PreferredPeerOrder contains each remote participant exactly once.
Which deployment configurations require at least two remote contributions and permit the proposed message-processing order.
How attempt validity is maintained when existing counters survive recovery or ballot changes; visible recovery and retry paths do not reset them.
What establishes the candidate-command association of the implicit local contribution across all relevant paths.
The applicable acceptance-support contract and an independent oracle connecting the commitment threshold to distinct participant acceptance.
audit_question.trigger_rationale: The newly attached source supplies an application-level source of repeated replies: handlePrepareReply invokes bcastAccept whenever prepareOKs+1 is at least ReadQuorumSize, without a one-shot phase guard. Additional equal-ballot prepare replies can therefore initiate additional Accept broadcasts. handleAccept replies on every invocation, and handleAcceptReply increments a scalar counter without visible contributor identity. This does not require assuming network duplication. A discriminating prospective schedule delivers multiple prepare replies, then processes replies to repeated Accept requests from one recipient before other recipients' acceptance. Whether that schedule can reach an insufficiently supported commitment depends on the actual quorum configuration and transport path, which require the requested source.

selection_rationale: Continue the same Fact-consumption question. The latest source resolves the previously unknown possibility of repeated sender-side emission: prepare completion is threshold-triggered on every qualifying reply, and recovery can reuse bookkeeping. The immediate discriminator is now whether separately generated replies from one recipient can satisfy a deployed write threshold before enough distinct recipients accept. This is more concrete than the still-unresolved different-command history and does not require changing the selected question or assuming network duplication. Source review must establish transport behavior, quorum applicability, and the acceptance-support contract before deriving an obligation. The paused short-commit question and its separately escalated wire-format child remain unchanged.
